text:
Jack Quinn is playing his way toward the most interesting contract in Buffalo, and The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn has already priced it out. The Sabres have bumped him to 18:57 a night (from 15:39) and put him on the ice for 79% of their power-play chances, and he has nine goals and 19 points in 21 games, up from 0.62 points a game to 0.90.

The goals are mostly earned, nine on 7.9 expected, and All Three Zones tracking put him in the 84th percentile for chances from the slot, with more than half his shots coming off the rush. If anything he's been unlucky: Buffalo has scored 7.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and he went pointless in his last two games despite nine shots.

The question for the contract is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice than with almost any forward last season (bottom 2%). His 5v5 share this year is a flat 50%. A team video headline after a loss to Dallas had him calling it "very frustrating." The Sabres haven't won in five.
headline: Jack Quinn's contract-year case
